summary: aicore ext conformance gets a new last scenario `crash`: a plugin that exits non-zero or dies by a signal while handling an invoke or event fails with evidence `call=...` and `exit_code=N` or `signal=NAME`, plus the remediation from the design. Skipped when an earlier call timed out. The CLI accepts `--manifest PATH` besides the positional manifest; giving both is an error and giving none exits 2. New fixtures: plugins `crash` (subscriber, exit 3) and `crash-signal` (command, SIGKILL), and subscriber `killed.py`. Tests copy fixtures into a fresh temp dir and run them by path, and test_delivery pins that a subscriber killed by SIGKILL leaves the cursor in place, sets pending PROCESS_EXIT, and redelivers the same event once fixed (delivery.py needed no change). Orch: new tests/test_native_conformance.py, all on fake argv: child-process-cleanup (grandchild gone after idle timeout, linger and cancel; a bystander in another session survives), stdout-stderr-framing (separate raw and .stderr files, failure detail from stderr only), and workspace-permissions (writes outside write_set are found from the git tree via scope.dirty/outside). These three scenarios are now `covered` for native with a ref in scenarios.json. For cao and claude-only they stay declared with a reason that names the orch parity trigger (ADR 0062). lock-expiry stays n/a with its existing reason. orch test_conformance.py and docs/conformance.md updated. Umbrella: `conformance` alias in configs/umbrella.json with routes plugin (aicore ext conformance) and engine (orch conformance), both found via provides.cli. scripts/umbrella.py prints a usage error (exit 2) when a known alias has no matching route. test-umbrella.py gets TestConformanceRoutes. Golden help cases recaptured. Both CHANGELOGs updated. Narrow tests all pass (see the list above).
